resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and Forest Lookouts (citing Ray Kresek) date abandonment to 1967. The 2010 Nez Perce National Forest list, which also cites Kresek among other sources, shows 1942 in the row beside 'abandoned'. The table layout does not make clear which column the year belongs to, so the story reports both dates and does not choose one.

firelookout.com calls it a 20-foot three-legged platform tower. Forest Lookouts calls it a 20-foot tree platform. The Forest Service list calls it a 20-foot three-legged tree platform. The story uses 'platform' and describes both forms as the sources give them.

notes_for_editor: The abandonment year is the main open question: 1967 (firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts citing Kresek) against 1942 in the Nez Perce NF list. The table layout puts '1942' twice in that row, once beside 'abandoned' and once in what looks like the photo column, so I could not be sure which is the abandonment date. The 1914 station and the 1939 platform may or may not be the same structure; the sources do not say, so the story presents them as separate entries. Forest Lookouts' Idaho County (M-W) page mentions a 1939 100-foot steel tower built by the Nezperce NF on a mountain I could not identify; it is not this site and is not used. No staffing history, access rules, or current description of the site was found. No photographs with direct image URLs were found.
